text: Write a class demonstrating that instance fields are per-object and static fields are per-class. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: Widget a = new Widget(), b = new Widget();
answer: private int mine = 0|private static int ours = 0|Widget.ours
explanation: Verified: `2 1 3`. Each object has its own `mine`; there is exactly one `ours` no matter how many objects exist. That is why a mutable static field is Chapter 23's strongest coupling and Chapter 31's worst concurrency hazard — everything touching it is coupled to everything else touching it, invisibly, and no lock is implied.
